cim: Dual Plane Orchestration Framework Optimizes Distributed Artificial Intelligence Pipelines Across Networks
cim_eredeti: Dual Plane Orchestration Framework Optimizes Distributed Artificial Intelligence Pipelines Across Networks
szoveg_eredeti:
Dual Plane Orchestration Framework Optimizes Distributed Artificial Intelligence Pipelines Across Networks

Telecommunications and computing researchers have formulated a mathematical model and algorithmic framework designed to orchestrate distributed artificial intelligence workloads across converged connect-compute networks. Published in the Journal of Network and Systems Management by researcher Roberto Riggio, the investigation addresses the operational challenge of deploying complex multi-stage machine learning pipelines across heterogeneous physical substrates spanning end-user devices, near-edge servers, far-edge clusters, and centralized clouds. The central architectural contribution formalizes the concept of Artificial Intelligence Functions, designated as modular and independently deployable software components that encapsulate individual stages of a machine learning workflow. To resolve the conflicting transmission requirements inherent in modern distributed computing, the framework establishes an explicit functional split separating an inference-focused data plane from a parameter-focused control plane. Experimental evaluations conducted across multiple substrate topologies demonstrated that an accompanying greedy heuristic achieves near-optimal resource placement costs while decreasing algorithmic computation times by three to four orders of magnitude compared to standard integer linear programming solutions.

The study positions its technical motivation within the rapid proliferation of artificial intelligence workloads across sectors such as automated mobility, healthcare, industrial automation, and immersive entertainment. These emerging applications integrate interdependent functional stages encompassing data acquisition, feature extraction, real-time inference, and centralized model consolidation. While fifth-generation mobile networks provide programmable connectivity fabrics through features like network slicing, multi-access edge computing, and disaggregated radio access, orchestrating non-monolithic machine learning pipelines across these fabrics remains challenging. Traditional orchestration architectures rooted in virtual network function and service function chain placement fail to capture the dual nature of modern artificial intelligence tasks. Existing paradigms typically model service requests as chains or directed acyclic graphs carrying a single class of uniform inter-component traffic. Consequently, standard frameworks cannot effectively reconcile the latency-critical streaming demands of live inference execution with the high-bandwidth, latency-tolerant bulk transfers required for centralized retraining, federated model parameter aggregation, drift-triggered updates, or canary rollouts.

To overcome these structural limitations, the published architecture introduces the formal reference model for Artificial Intelligence Functions, which are treated as first-class orchestratable building blocks. Each function encapsulates an individual pipeline stage, ranging from lightweight sensor filtering and video anonymization to computationally intensive neural network inference and federated averaging. Every unit exposes four distinct operational interfaces to govern execution and communication. The northbound interface, designated if1, provides an application-level configuration entry point through which external orchestration managers or human operators dynamically update runtime parameters, such as loaded model architectures, inference batch sizes, and telemetry reporting intervals. The westbound communication mechanisms are divided into two dedicated channels: the if3 interface handles the machine learning data plane, carrying continuous streaming payload between successive processing stages, while the if2 interface manages the machine learning control plane, exchanging model parameters, gradient updates, distilled representations, and distribution statistics across participating nodes.

The operational split between the data plane and the control plane reflects systematic divergences in bandwidth, periodicity, latency tolerance, and underlying communication topologies. The investigation establishes that the data plane carries ordered, high-bandwidth, latency-critical inference traffic, exemplified by raw video streams passing through anonymization filters, object detectors, and downstream actuators. This pipeline traffic demands strict sub-hundred-millisecond latencies and is characterized by a strictly acyclic dependency flow where downstream stages cannot proceed without upstream outputs. In contrast, the control plane carries episodic bulk transmissions of model state dispatched at intervals ranging from seconds to hours, accommodating latencies up to several seconds without degrading application correctness. Furthermore, control plane flows often form cyclic or hub-and-spoke topologies, such as edge nodes transmitting local weights to a centralized consolidation server that periodically redistributes updated global models. The author notes that split inference, wherein intermediate activations of a single partitioned model are transmitted between nodes, is classified under the data plane because intermediate activations represent continuous request-specific payloads that strictly gate execution progress.

To illustrate the expressive range of the model, the publication details two representative industrial use cases. The first examines a pedestrian crossing warning system designed to detect approaching vehicles and trigger acoustic or visual alarms in real time. The corresponding application graph connects five functions: a camera-anchored video ingestion unit, an obfuscation component that blurs faces and license plates for privacy compliance, a hardware-accelerated feature extraction unit running object detection, an actuation interface controlling physical crossing signals, and a cloud-hosted consolidation engine managing federated learning updates. The second use case targets adaptive video streaming using the MPEG Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over HTTP protocol. In this deployment, telemetry functions interface with an Open Radio Access Network Near-Real-Time Radio Access Network Intelligent Controller via the A1 interface to monitor physical channel conditions. Co-located bitrate prediction models process radio measurements to forecast client throughput, directing proactive chunk selection at a central media server while cloud-based update functions push revised model weights downstream over control plane links.

At the formal level, the framework represents application requirements as an Artificial Intelligence Forwarding Graph, defined as a directed multigraph where vertices denote individual functions and edges represent typed virtual links. Virtual link edges are explicitly constructed over typed triples to accommodate parallel edges connecting the same pair of functions, permitting an inference payload link and a parameter exchange link to share endpoints while retaining independent QoS constraints, bandwidth specifications, and latency budgets. The underlying physical infrastructure is modeled as a directed substrate graph where physical nodes possess multi-dimensional capacity vectors tracking central processing units, memory, storage, and specialized hardware acceleration units such as graphical processing units. Physical links are characterized by propagation latencies and available bandwidth capacities. Each substrate element is further assigned per-unit operational costs and fixed activation costs, establishing the financial and resource baseline against which workload mappings are mathematically optimized.

The paper formalizes the global mapping challenge as an Integer Linear Programming model aimed at minimizing the cumulative placement cost while satisfying capacity, mapping uniqueness, semantic anchoring, latency, and multi-commodity flow conservation constraints.
